title: Lichen planus
summary: Itchy, flat-topped, purple, polygonal papules on the wrists, shins and lower back, often with white lacy streaks in the mouth. Mostly self-limiting on the skin; oral and genital erosive disease needs specialist care.

glance.think: Intensely itchy purple flat-topped papules with fine white lines (Wickham striae), on the wrists, ankles or lower back; lacy white patches in the mouth.
glance.engine: T-cell-mediated attack on basal keratinocytes (interface dermatitis); hepatitis C and drugs (lichenoid eruptions) are associations.
glance.backbone: Potent topical steroid, sedating antihistamine at night if needed, review drugs; refer oral, genital, nail or scalp disease.
glance.never_miss: Erosive oral or genital LP (SCC risk), lichen planopilaris (scarring hair loss) and nail destruction.

what: **Lichen planus (LP)** is an idiopathic inflammatory disorder of skin and/or mucosa presenting with intensely itchy **flat-topped, violaceous, polygonal papules**. Classic cutaneous LP favours **flexor wrists**, lumbar back, ankles. Mucosal, nail, scalp (lichen planopilaris), and genital variants exist. Association with **hepatitis C** is described in some populations — screen selectively by risk/prevalence.

list: T-cell mediated attack on basal keratinocytes (lichenoid interface dermatitis).

Triggers: idiopathic; drugs (**lichenoid drug eruption** — e.g. some antihypertensives, antimalarials, gold, TNF inhibitors — take drug history); dental amalgam sometimes linked to oral LP; HCV association variable by region.

head: Feature
Detail
rows: Violaceous, planar, polygonal, pruritic papules ± plaques (“6 Ps”); Wickham striae (white lace) on surface
Flexor wrists, lumbar, ankles, shins; genitals; oral (reticular white network, erosions)
Marked hyperpigmentation, especially skin of colour

list: Full exam: skin, mouth, nails, scalp, genitals.
**Punch biopsy** if uncertain (band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, saw-tooth acanthosis, civatte bodies).
Consider HCV testing based on risk/local guidance; drug review for lichenoid drug eruption.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Coin plaques, less violaceous polygonal papules

list: Potent / very potent **TCS** ointments to itchy papules (short courses; caution thin skin); emollients.
Oral / genital / nail / extensive / scarring scalp disease → **dermatology** (may need systemic steroids, phototherapy, or other immunosuppressants — specialist).
Oral LP: topical steroid mouth preparations per dental/oral medicine pathways; check malignancy vigilance for persistent ulcers.
Stop culprit drug if lichenoid drug eruption suspected (with prescriber of that drug).

red_flags: Non-healing oral ulcer, white patch that thickens or a lump in long-standing oral LP: **refer urgently** (oral SCC).
Genital erosions, scarring or dyspareunia: refer (vulval or penile LP).
Scalp redness with scarring hair loss: lichen planopilaris, early referral.
pearls: Warn about post-inflammatory pigment lasting months.
Advise against vigorous scrubbing of Wickham-striae scale.
Sexual health / genital itch: examine and refer early if erosive.
Document HCV risk discussion where relevant.
